userProblem: I can read about rotating magnetic fields but cannot predict what frequency changes mean or distinguish synchronous speed from rotor speed.

source.title: Synthetic motor teaching passage
source.text: In a three-phase induction motor the stator field rotates at synchronous speed. For frequency f in hertz and P stator poles, synchronous speed in revolutions per minute is n_s = 120 f / P. The rotor normally runs below synchronous speed when it produces torque; the difference is called slip. The formula predicts the rotating field's synchronous speed, not a measured shaft speed or a guarantee of a specific rotor speed under load.

questions.prompt: Before you look at an answer, predict the synchronous speed of the field for 50 Hz and 4 poles.
questions.rubric: Use n_s = 120 f / P, substituting 50 Hz and 4 poles; record attempted reasoning before showing worked answer.

questions.prompt: With the same four poles, what happens when frequency changes to 60 Hz?
questions.rubric: Correct synchronous speed 1800 rpm, an increase of 300 rpm; do not promise actual shaft speed equals 1800.

questions.prompt: Keep 50 Hz but choose six poles. Predict the synchronous speed.
questions.rubric: Correct synchronous speed 1000 rpm; it decreases with higher pole count.

criticalMisconceptions: Synchronous speed is not measured rotor speed.
Slip and load matter for actual rotor operating speed.
